questions.q_en: Pritam buys rice at the rate of Rs. 15/kg. He sells it to Rhitam at 20% profit. However his faulty balance shows 1 kg when it is actually 850 gm. Rhitam bought 20 Kgs of rice from Pritam. What is the overall profit (in Rs.) that Pritam makes?
questions.solution_en:
Pritam sells rice to Rhitam at a price of = (15+20% of 15)= Rs.18/kg.

Now Rhitam bought 20 Kgs from Pritam at a total price of =Rs. 18*20 =Rs. 360

But as Pritam has a faulty balance thus he is actually selling 850*20/100=17Kgs instead of 20 Kgs.

Pritam buys 17kgs of rice at a total price of =Rs.17*15 =Rs. 255 and sells it to Rhitam at a price of Rs.360

So Total profit that Pritam makes =Rs. (360 - 255) =Rs. 105.

questions.q_en: A train of length 180 m passes a 320 m platform in 40 s, then meets and crosses an oncoming train of length L m moving at 54 km/h in 12 s. Find L.
questions.solution_en:
First train's speed = (180+320)/40 = 500/40 = 25/2 m/s

Opposing train speed = 54 * 5/18 = 15 m/s

Relative speed = 25/2 + 15 = 55/2 m/s

Crossing time = 12 s

Distance = (55/2) X 12 = 330 m

Hence, 180 + L = 330

L = 150 m

questions.q_en: The area of a square is 1024 sq.m. What is the perimeter of a rectangle whose length is twice the side of the square and the breadth is half the side of the square?
questions.solution_en:
Let 's' be the side of the square.

Area of the square = s2 = 1024 sq m

s = √1024 = 32 m

Therefore length of the rectangle = 2*32 = 64 m

Therefore breadth of the rectangle = (1/2)*32 = 16 m

Therefore perimeter of the rectangle = 2*(64 + 16) = 160 m.

questions.q_en: In a race, Rani beats Vani by 252 m or 36 seconds. If the speed of Rani is 10 m/s, then find the speed of Vani.
questions.solution_en:
Let the speed of Vani = X m/s and length of race course = L meters

Speed of Rani = 10 m/s

L/10 = (L - 252)/X

X = 10(L - 252)/L -------(1)

and

L/X - L/10 = 36

X = L/(36 + L/10) ------(2)

From equation (1) and (2)-

10(L - 252)/L = L/(36 + L/10)

(L - 252)(360 + L) = L2

108L = 252*360

L = 840

X = 840/(36 + 840/10)

X = 840/120

X = 7 m/s

Hence, the speed of Vani = 7 m/s

questions.q_en: A 240 m long train overtakes a man walking at 6 km/h in the same direction, in 9 seconds. How much time (in seconds) will it take to pass a 372 m long tunnel with the same speed?
questions.solution_en:
Let the speed of the train = p m/s

Speed of man = 6 km/h = 6 * 5/18 = 5/3 m/s

According to the question-

(p - 5/3) * 9 = 240

p - 5/3 = 80/3

p = 80/3 + 5/3

p = 85/3 m/s

Total distance = 240 + 372 = 612 m

Time =612/(85/3)=(612*3)/85

Time = 21.6 seconds

questions.q_en: ∆STU is right-angled at T. Points V and W are on side ST such that SV: VW: WT = 1: 2: 3 respectively. Points X and Y are on side SU such that VX || WY || TU. If length of side TU is 48 cm, then what is (VX + WY) equal to?
questions.solution_en:
SV: VW: WT = 1: 2: 3

Let SV = a cm, VW = 2a cm, and WT = 3a cm

∆SVX, ∆SWY, and ∆STU are similar triangles.

In ∆SVX and ∆STU,

VX/TU = SV/ST

VX = 48 * a/(a + 2a + 3a) = 8 cm

Now in ∆SWY, and ∆STU,

WY/TU = SW/ST

=> WY = 48 * (a + 2a)/(a + 2a + 3a) = 24 cm

Hence, VX + WY = 8 + 24 = 32 cm

questions.q_en: A six-digit number 11p9q4 is divisible by 24. Then the greatest possible value for pq is:
questions.solution_en:
A number is divisible by 24 means a number is divisible by both 3 and 8 individually.

11p9q4 is divisible by 8 means last three digits (9q4) must be divisible by 8.

Possible values of q = 0, 4, 8 [We cannot take 0 as a value of 'q' because it will make the product 0 and we will never get the maximum possible value.]

When q = 4:

Sum of digits of number = 1 + 1 + p + 9 + 4 + 4 = 19 + p

Possible values of p = 2, 5, 8

Possible values of 'pq' = 8, 20, 32

When q = 8:

Sum of digits of number = 1 + 1 + p + 9 + 8 + 4 = 23 + p

Possible values of p = 1, 4, 7

Possible values of 'pq' = 8, 32, 56

So, maximum possible value of 'pq' = 56

questions.q_en: A vendor sells his goods using weights 19% less than true weights and makes a profit of 35%. His net gain percentage (rounded off to 2 decimal places) is:
questions.solution_en:
True weight = 100 g, false weight = 81 g.

Cost for 81 g = 81C,

SP for "100 g" with 35% profit = 1.35 X 81C.

Normally, SP for 100 g = 1.35 X 100C = 135C.

False weight SP = 135C for 81 g,

profit = 135C - 81C = 54C.

Gain % = (54C / 81C) X 100 = 66.67%.

Option (a) is the correct answer.
